translation: Target is the following proposition: for every set K of closed arithmetic sentences, if every member of K is true in the standard natural numbers, then at least one of two alternatives holds: (1) there is no recursively enumerable set F of arithmetic axioms such that K is exactly the set of sentences derivable from F; or (2) there exists a closed arithmetic sentence σ that is syntactically Π₁ in the library’s sense, is true in the standard natural numbers, and has neither σ nor its formal negation in K. K is not assumed to be deductively closed. The second alternative concerns nonmembership in K, not nonderivability from K, and no Π₁ condition is imposed on the negation of σ.

divergences.description: Koellner’s displayed Claim 3 does not restrict φ to Π⁰₁. Lean adds that restriction: strict inclusion in T alone gives a missing truth but does not specify its complexity. The restriction reflects the Diophantine motivation without literally requiring σ to assert that a particular polynomial equation has no solution.

Lean generalizes from the intended K of humanly provable sentences to every sound set of arithmetic sentences. This includes sets that are not deductively closed, for which the first disjunct holds automatically because K cannot equal a full theorem set.

judgement.summary: The explicit soundness premise matches K ⊆ T, and Lean preserves both the exact equality in the first disjunct and the two nonmembership conditions in the second. The result is a uniform, Π⁰₁-refined version of Claim 3.
